name: IL-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Mary Miller with large financial advantage
Challenger raised only ~$113k with no outside support
model.rationale: The R+20 lean, Miller's incumbency and roughly 12-to-1 fundraising edge leave Jennifer Todd with no evident path; markets price the Republican near 96%. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals-implied margin, with only a slight environment adjustment.
model.watch: A major Democratic outside-spending intervention or a scandal involving Miller could narrow the race, though neither is currently evident.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
This rural southern Illinois district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of roughly R+20. Mary Miller, the incumbent, is running for reelection and holds a decisive financial advantage, having raised about $1.3 million with over $800,000 on hand. Her Democratic challenger, Jennifer Todd, has raised only about $113,000 and has no reported outside support.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price the Republican at roughly 96 percent. The favorable environment for the party out of power in 2026 trims the expected margin slightly, but the seat remains firmly in Republican hands absent an unforeseen development.
